```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Lower trust barrier for a first sale. B's brief lists sourced regulatory needs: a DPA, a privacy policy and records of processing, all one-time drafts with periodic review. A's brief says buyers commercially expect SOC2-type assurance, which needs a licensed CPA audit, plus migration help and tax-season support. That is a heavy credibility load for one operator trying to close a first customer in 90 days.",
    "Lower cost of failure for the buyer. A feedback widget that misbehaves is an annoyance. A bookkeeping tool that misbehaves touches bank data and tax filings. That makes a first customer more likely to try an unknown solo vendor in B.",
    "Willingness to pay is better documented in B. A third-party study of 62 priced tools puts the median cheapest paid plan at $31.50/mo, and Canny, Frill and Userback show paid tiers. A's pricing anchors are only two competitors, and its own case against says free tiers (Kick) likely already cover typical solo-founder volumes.",
    "B's case for cites a working example of the operating model. Upstep markets AI-agent triage via MCP, which suggests a one-person, agent-run build of a narrow wedge is feasible within the timeline.",
    "Both categories are saturated: six-plus competitors in A, 73 tracked tools in B. So saturation does not separate them, and the decision comes down to trust burden and time-to-first-sale, where B is better."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's key quantification of the pain, Growthy's estimate of $400-600/mo in bookkeeper time per Stripe-connected client, has no citation or link. It should be treated as unsourced. Without it, A's demand case rests on three anecdotal quotes. One of those (\"I hired someone\") shows willingness to pay for a human bookkeeper, not software. Another comes from someone who already built a competing tool.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. A has somewhat richer demand evidence: three pain quotes, including a 3-4 hours/month time cost. B's demand evidence is thinner: one quote from a builder of a competing tool and one buyer complaining that prices are too high, which cuts against willingness to pay. B wins mainly because its trust and compliance burden for a first sale is lower, not because its demand is clearly proven. Both briefs describe crowded markets with no identified wedge."
}
```
